toc.title: Transparency, explainability, documentation tools, trade-offs and human-centered design

html:
1What You Will Learn

  • Tell transparent and explainable models from those that are not
  • Name the tools: SageMaker Model Cards, AI Service Cards and Bedrock Model Evaluation
  • Weigh open source models, data and licensing
  • Describe the trade-offs between safety, transparency, interpretability and performance
  • Apply human-centered design for explainable AI

2Transparency, explainability, documentation tools, trade-offs and human-centered design

Running case

Cedar and Salt Must Explain Itself

  • A guest is refused a loyalty reward by an AI model and asks why
  • Regulators and auditors ask what the model is for, and how it was tested
  • The team can choose between a simple model and a more accurate complex one
  • Your job: choose models, documents and designs that let people understand

Transparent, Explainable and Opaque Models

Kind of model What you can know
Transparent How it was built: data, design and limits are documented and open to review
Explainable Why it gave an output, such as which features mattered, even for a complex model
Neither (opaque or black box) Little is disclosed, and no reasons can be given
  • AWS describes explainability as understanding and evaluating system outputs, and transparency as letting people make informed choices about an AI system
  • Why it matters: trust, debugging, audits and regulation, and fair treatment of people

Exam tip: Transparent is about how it was built; explainable is about why it answered.

Amazon SageMaker Model Cards

  • Model Cards document a model's critical details in one place, for governance and reporting
  • Intended uses: what it is for, and what it is not for, plus the assumptions made
  • Risk rating: unknown, low, medium or high
  • Training details and metrics, evaluation results, and caveats and recommendations
  • Edits create new versions, an immutable record; export as PDF to share
  • They support audits, guidance on use, and links to business goals

Exam tip: One document for a model's purpose, risk, training and evaluation: SageMaker Model Cards.

AI Service Cards and Other Transparency Tools

Tool What it gives you
AWS AI Service Cards A single place for intended use cases, limitations, responsible AI design choices and performance best practices of AWS AI services
SageMaker Clarify Explanations of which input features drove a prediction
Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation Evidence of quality, toxicity, robustness and faithfulness
Knowledge Bases source attribution The sources behind a RAG answer

Exam tip: Model Cards document your own models; AI Service Cards describe AWS's services.

Open Source Models, Data and Licensing Beyond the guide

  • Open models let you inspect, host and adapt the model, so they are often more transparent
  • Open does not mean unrestricted or safe: read the license for commercial use and limits
  • Ask for the training data: its sources, categories and licenses
  • Closed models may disclose only a model card or service card
  • Document your choices in a Model Card, and evaluate every model on your own task

Exam tip: Check the license and the data before you adopt any model.

Trade-Offs: Safety, Transparency, Interpretability and Performance Beyond the guide

Trade-off The tension
Interpretability and performance Simple models are easier to explain; complex models often perform better but are harder to explain
Safety and transparency Openness helps audits and trust; revealing too much, such as safety rules, can help attackers
  • Measure both: track interpretability and performance, and pick the balance the risk allows
  • High-stakes decisions about people lean toward explainable models and human review

Exam tip: Simple and explainable versus complex and accurate: weigh both against the risk.

Human-Centered Design for Explainable AI Beyond the guide

  • Design with users, not only for them
  • AI decision transparency: say when AI is used, show sources and reasons, and state limits
  • User feedback mechanisms: ratings, corrections and ways to report problems
  • Human oversight: let people review, challenge and escalate; Amazon A2I supports human review
  • Learn from feedback to improve the system

Exam tip: Tell users when AI is used, show why, and give them a way to respond.

What the Exam Asks: Transparency and Explainability

  • Which kind of model: transparent, explainable or neither
  • Which tool: SageMaker Model Cards, Bedrock Model Evaluation, AI Service Cards or Clarify
  • Which source: open source models, data and licensing
  • Which trade-off: interpretability versus performance, or safety versus transparency
  • Which design principle: user feedback and decision transparency

Exam tip: Name the need first: document, explain, evaluate or involve users.

Design Check: Cedar and Salt Explains Itself

What the team needs Name and answer
Record a model's purpose, risk and test results for auditors SageMaker Model Card
Show a guest why the model refused a reward An explainable model, with Clarify feature explanations
Evidence of quality and toxicity before launch Bedrock Model Evaluation
Choose an open source model for hosting Check license, training data and evaluate it
Simple but weaker or complex but strong for rewards Weigh interpretability against performance; add human review
Let guests flag wrong answers User feedback mechanism
  • Cover the right column, answer each row yourself, then compare

3Exam Q&A

3.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1Which AWS tool documents a model's intended uses, risk rating, training details and evaluation results in one place?

  • AAmazon SageMaker Model Cards, which document a model's use and risk
  • BAmazon Bedrock Guardrails, which filter harmful content in prompts
  • CAWS Config, which records resource configurations and their changes
  • DAmazon Macie, which finds sensitive data stored in Amazon S3 buckets
Show the answer

Answer: A. SageMaker Model Cards document critical details about a model for governance and reporting, including intended uses, risk rating, training details and evaluation results. Guardrails filters content, Config tracks configuration, and Macie finds sensitive data.

S2Which statement best describes an explainable model?

  • AIt never changes its answers between runs
  • BIt is always smaller than other models
  • CIt can give reasons for why it produced an output
  • DIt was trained only on data that is public
Show the answer

Answer: C. Explainability means people can understand why a model produced an output, for example which input features mattered. It is about reasons, not size, repeatability or the source of the training data.

S3Which TWO features help users trust an AI application? (Select TWO.)

  • AA way for users to give feedback on answers
  • BHiding that an AI model produced the response
  • CTelling users when AI was used and showing sources
  • DRemoving all reasons from the answers it gives
  • EDisabling every route to reach a human reviewer
Show the answer

Answer: A, C. Human-centered design for explainable AI includes user feedback mechanisms and decision transparency, such as disclosing AI use and showing sources. Hiding AI use, removing reasons and blocking human review reduce trust.

S4Cedar and Salt must explain reward decisions to guests and is choosing between model types. Which trade-off should the team weigh?

  • AComplex models are always much easier to interpret than every simple model can be
  • BSimpler models are easier to interpret, but complex ones often perform better
  • CInterpretability and performance never affect each other in any real model choice
  • DTransparency does not matter at all when AI models make decisions about people
Show the answer

Answer: B. Simpler models are generally easier to interpret, while complex models often achieve higher performance but are harder to explain. For decisions that affect people, weigh both, measure both and add human review.

4Quick Reference Card

  • Transparent is how it was built; explainable is why it answered
  • Tools: SageMaker Model Cards, AI Service Cards, Clarify and Bedrock Model Evaluation
  • Open models: check the license and the training data
  • Trade-offs: interpretability against performance; safety against transparency
  • Human-centered design: feedback, decision transparency and human oversight
